source.title: Encoder-Decoder or Decoder-Only? Revisiting Encoder-Decoder Large Language Model
source.authors: Biao Zhang; Yong Cheng; Siamak Shakeri; Xin-Yi Wang; Min Ma; Orhan Firat

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and figure labels are garbled in extraction, but the relevant exponents are readable in Table 1b.
record.tranche_reason: It measures held-out perplexity across model sizes and training compute, fits scaling exponents, and evaluates downstream scores at multiple scales using a scaling study related to the original measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out perplexity scaling results and downstream scores by model size. Its compute-optimal isoFLOP results are plotted in Figure 13, but numerical optimal parameter/token allocations are not stated. Detailed per-task downstream results in Figures 14–16 are not separately extracted; cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws of held-out perplexity against parameters (150M–8B) and training FLOPs for decoder-only (DecLLM) and encoder-decoder (RedLLM) models, on in-domain RedPajama and out-of-domain Paloma. It also reports downstream averages across five scales. The method matches the original measurement, applied to a new encoder-decoder setting. The study's aim is architecture comparison, not a test of scaling laws themselves.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find RedLLM and DecLLM have similar scaling exponents, with DecLLM dominating the compute-optimal frontier and pretraining zero/few-shot results. After instruction tuning, RedLLM matches or beats DecLLM with much better inference efficiency. They also report RedLLM's stronger context-length extrapolation, and that PPL fails to predict downstream adaptability.
record.recipe_differences: Uses held-out PPL scaling analyses similar to the cited scaling-law work, but compares newly trained encoder-decoder and decoder-only models using different pretraining objectives and a specific RedPajama/Paloma setup; it is not an explicit replication of either named source.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported fitted exponents vary across the RedPajama and Paloma evaluation datasets and between RedLLM and DecLLM. Downstream results vary between pretraining and FLAN instruction tuning, and with bidirectional input attention.

fits_no_version.finding: Encoder-decoder and decoder-only models share similar power-law exponents but differ in offset. DecLLM has lower PPL at equal parameters, while at equal FLOPs the curves nearly overlap. DecLLM dominates the compute-optimal frontier at larger budgets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture family (encoder-decoder vs decoder-only, with matched objectives) shifts the scaling-law coefficient and compute frontier but not the exponent.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the fitted exponents or downstream averages. Architecture and pretraining objective differ together between RedLLM and DecLLM, complicating attribution. The compute-optimal allocation results are plotted but not numerically tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's Figure 13 compute-optimal isoFLOP curves and markers are not numerically extracted; the paper does not state numerical optimal parameter/token growth exponents. Per-task results in Figures 14–16 are omitted to prioritize the average downstream results in Table 2; they exceed the remaining row allowance if recorded separately.

untested.parts: Token-count scaling. All models are trained to the same ~1.6T tokens, so data is not varied as an axis. The parameter range spans under two orders of magnitude.
No extrapolation from small fits to held-out larger runs.

A Hoffmann-style compute-optimal fit and isoFLOP slices at 1e20, 1e21 and 5e21 FLOPs are plotted (Fig 13). No allocation exponents or optimal N/D are reported, so stability of the split cannot be judged.
Depth and width are not varied at fixed parameter count.
No other modality is tested. Fine-tuning is scored only on downstream tasks, not with loss power laws.
Parameter counting, training schedule, fitting method and curvature are not varied.

missing.what: Compute-optimal isoFLOP minima for RedLLM and DecLLM at three budgets (positions of the ⋆ markers)
Statement that RedLLM 8B and DecLLM 4B have comparable PPL but very different zero/few-shot scores
missing.locator: Section 5, 'RedLLM scales slightly for few-shot learning'

missing.what: Fitted law coefficients and offsets (e.g. negative offsets in Fig 2 legends), partly garbled in extraction

record.verdict_notes: The fits are on perplexity, evaluated with a prefix-LM split (1024 prefix + 1024 target), not on raw loss. All models share a fixed 400K-step, 1.6T-token run, so FLOPs scaling is confounded with parameter scaling. No uncertainties are reported. RedLLM and DecLLM also differ in objective (prefix vs causal LM) and in effective target tokens (0.8T vs 1.6T). Single-scale ds rows only carry information as series.

versions.untested_parts: Training-token scaling with parameters and compute held non-bottlenecking is not separately fitted; the reported fits are for parameters and training FLOPs.
No explicit test is reported in which fits from small runs predict held-out, much larger runs.
The paper fits compute-optimal scaling laws and shows isoFLOP plots, but does not state numerical parameter- or token-growth exponents or tabulate optimal allocations.
Depth, width, and other architectural details are not varied at fixed parameter count to test their effect on loss.
No other modality, repeated-data regime, or fine-tuning/transfer loss power law is tested.
The paper reports average downstream scores across scale, but does not fit a predictive law from pretraining loss or test forecasts on held-out model scales.
The study compares architectures and evaluation datasets, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, or fitting method, nor test curvature away from a single power law.

relationships.condition: Held-out PPL vs parameters (150M–8B) and training FLOPs, DecLLM and RedLLM, in-domain RedPajama and out-of-domain Paloma
relationships.reason: Power-law fits with exponents 0.17–0.27 are reported for all eight combinations (sc1–sc8), and the authors call the out-of-domain behaviour consistent. No fit-quality or CI is given.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out perplexity followed reported power-law fits with exponents of 0.17–0.27 across all eight architecture, resource and domain combinations.

source_check.condition: Held-out PPL vs parameters (150M–8B) and training FLOPs, DecLLM and RedLLM, in-domain RedPajama and out-of-domain Paloma
source_check.reason: Table 1b and Figures 2 and 10 report power-law fits for PPL. V1 specifies held-out pretraining loss; the text does not establish a power law for that quantity. Figure 11 separately reports training loss without the required held-out loss fits.

relationships.condition: Choice of evaluation dataset (RedPajama vs Paloma)
relationships.reason: Exponents rise by 0.02–0.04 on Paloma (sc1 vs sc5, sc2 vs sc6, sc3 vs sc7, sc4 vs sc8), so they depend on eval data. The differences are small and have no uncertainty, and architecture barely changes them.
relationships.display_finding: Exponents rise by 0.02–0.04 on Paloma, with little architectural variation and no reported uncertainty for these small differences.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Choice of evaluation dataset (RedPajama vs Paloma)
source_check.reason: Table 1b confirms that changing evaluation corpus increases all four fitted exponents by 0.02–0.04. This supports evaluation-dependent point estimates; no uncertainty establishes the significance of these differences.

relationships.condition: DecLLM pretrained, and all models after FLAN instruction tuning
relationships.reason: Average scores rise with size: DecLLM pretrained zero-shot 21.14→31.13 and few-shot 26.21→43.37; tuned models roughly 30→60. There is one small dip in ds49.
relationships.display_finding: Pretrained DecLLM averages rose from 21.14 to 31.13 zero-shot and 26.21 to 43.37 few-shot, while tuned models rose roughly from 30 to 60, with one small dip.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: DecLLM pretrained, and all models after FLAN instruction tuning
source_check.reason: Table 2 confirms increasing average downstream performance across model sizes for pretrained DecLLM and all finetuned families, apart from the small few-shot DecLLM + BiAttn dip from 56.52 to 55.95. These are observed scaling trends rather than validated extrapolations.

relationships.reason: Zero-shot is nearly flat (ds1–ds5, 18.11→20.04) and few-shot gains are slight and non-monotonic (ds11–ds15), even though PPL falls as a power law.
relationships.display_finding: Zero-shot scores rose only from 18.11 to 20.04, and few-shot gains were slight and nonmonotonic despite power-law perplexity reductions.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Table 2 shows weak zero-shot improvement, 18.11 to 20.04, and smaller, non-monotonic few-shot improvement, 26.51 to 35.13. Section 5 explicitly describes limited downstream scaling despite improving PPL.

relationships.condition: Predicting downstream scores from pretraining PPL across architectures (text-based, no row)
relationships.reason: The authors state RedLLM 8B and DecLLM 4B have comparable PPL, yet RedLLM lags far downstream. They add that PPL 'fails to capture a model's adaptability'. This rests on the text, not on a row.
relationships.display_finding: RedLLM 8B substantially underperformed DecLLM 4B downstream despite comparable pretraining perplexity.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Predicting downstream scores from pretraining PPL across architectures (text-based, no row)
source_check.reason: Within this condition group the authors explicitly report failure of PPL to capture adaptability. Section 5 identifies comparable PPL for RedLLM 8B and DecLLM 4B despite substantially different downstream scores; Section 6 also reports that worse pretraining performance can precede better finetuned performance.
